profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Smallest workload / floor probe: 2048 output elements, latency 0.11450ms vs reference 0.04954ms (speedup 0.433), isolates the fixed per-call overhead term.

Mid-size launch-bound representative: latency 0.10584ms vs reference 0.02536ms (speedup 0.240); 524288 elements copied yet device kernel only 3.13us -- the clearest speedup-loss case among flat-variant workloads.
Worst measured workload (speedup 0.213) and the persistent-variant representative: latency 0.10964ms vs reference 0.02335ms.
Largest workload and the only regime where candidate matches the reference (speedup 1.036); device-bound control that must not regress if the next experiment targets host overhead.

findings.label: Small/mid workloads are launch/dispatch bound: device kernel is <7% of measured walltime
findings.inference: For float32::0 the kernel executes in 1.52us but eval walltime is 114.5us (0.11450ms), and 100 invocations advance the device ~130us apart (op_summary task start timestamps 5108603, 5109073, 5109207, 5109338, 5109470 ... deltas ~112-135us) while each kernel runs only 1.5-3.5us, so the vector core sits idle >=94% of every interval. Same shape for float32::2 (kernel 3.13us vs eval 105.8us) and bfloat16::3 (kernel 7.61us vs eval 109.6us). The constant ~0.09-0.16ms eval floor across n=2048..33.5M is therefore a fixed per-call launch/host cost, not device copy work; the ~110us Task Wait Time per invocation is the artifact-level signal of that gap.

findings.label: Variant selection is as coded; small workloads launch tiny grids (1 and 32 blocks) but that does not drive walltime
findings.inference: Consistent with the seed source: float32::0 n=2048 -> BLOCK=2048, nblocks=1 (<128) -> _narrow_copy_flat_kernel with grid=1, i.e. 1 of 20 AICores; float32::2 n=524288 -> BLOCK=16384, nblocks=32 -> flat, grid=32; bfloat16::3 n=8388608 -> nblocks=512 (>=128) -> persistent, grid clamped to 40; float16::4 -> persistent, reported Block Num=40 (host computes grid=min(256,max(40,2048//13))=157, so the reported 40 may reflect a hardware concurrency cap). Because these kernels complete in 1.5-7.6us, grid occupancy or persistent-loop occupancy cannot move walltime for these workloads, so grid/block tuning is not the lever.

findings.label: Largest workload is MTE-bandwidth bound and already at reference parity (control regime)
findings.inference: Copies 512x65536 fp16 (67MB read + 67MB write). Kernel 89-90us steady state ~= eval walltime 100.26us, so here device time dominates and the launch floor is hidden. aiv_mte2_ratio 0.95 is near DMA saturation and aiv_vec_ratio ~0 means the vector ALU is idle: pure data movement at the memory roofline, which is why eval speedup is 1.036 (candidate ~ reference 103.85us) and why no host-side change can improve this workload materially.

performance_interpretation: Round 1 (seed) geo_mean=0.377, min_speedup=0.213. msprof metrics on 4 workloads (small=float32::0 [64,64] dim0 s16 l32, mid=float32::2 [1024,1024] s256 l512, worst=bfloat16::3 [4096,4096] s1024 l2048, largest/control=float16::4 [1024,65536] s256 l512) split the 15 timing workloads into two regimes. (A) 12 of 15 workloads are launch/dispatch bound: the device kernel is tiny (1.52us, 3.13us, 7.61us) while eval walltime is ~105-115us, i.e. 98-99% of the measured time is per-call non-kernel cost (host dispatch/launch/queue wait), not device copy; op_summary Task Wait Time between successive kernel starts is ~110-160us while each kernel runs 1.5-7.6us. (B) The 3 largest 2-D workloads (the [1024,65536] family, float16::4 verified) are device memory-bandwidth bound: kernel ~106us avg (89-90us steady state) ~= eval 100.3us with aiv_mte2_ratio=0.95 / aiv_mte3_ratio=0.80, and there the candidate is already at reference parity (speedup 1.036). So the seed copy algorithm is correct and measurable, but the frozen hypothesis' implied optimization premise (copy/division design) is contradicted for ~80% of workloads; the binding limit is the per-call launch/host floor (~110us) versus the reference floor (~22-50us). The profiler cannot decompose host Python/Triton-launch vs device SQ task-dispatch latency at metrics level (execution-trace.json carries only device kernel events and HostToDevice flow edges, no host-side python/aten durations), so the discriminating experiment must be run on the candidate.

next_experiment.action_description: Attack the fixed ~110us per-call launch/dispatch floor for the 12 launch-bound workloads: in run() add a cached launch plan keyed on (dtype, shape, dim, start, length, strides, device) that stores out_shape as a tuple, base_in, BLOCK, the grid tuple, EVEN and the already-selected kernel object, so steady-state calls perform zero Python loops/type coercion and issue exactly one pre-resolved Triton launch plus torch.empty. Keep the existing generic path as the fallback whenever the key misses or strides are non-canonical. Do not touch the kernel bodies or the MTE-bound large-copy path.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the flat 0.09-0.16ms floor is host-side launch overhead, small/mid latencies should fall from ~105-115us toward the reference floor (~22-50us), lifting geo_mean from 0.377 toward >=0.50 and potentially much higher on the sizes where the reference is 22-25us; float16::4 (~100us MTE-bound) must stay unchanged.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: A stale cache key would silently drop elements/rows and break correctness, so the key must include strides+dtype+device and non-canonical inputs must always fall back. The cache also adds complexity for no gain if the floor is device SQ dispatch. Rollback: restore the seed run() verbatim (workspace is not a git repo, so keep the seed text).
success_criteria: Full eval stays correct: all correctness workloads PASSED and all 15 timing workloads PASSED with no matched_ratio/error regression.
float32::0 and float32::2 latency drop materially (e.g. <=0.07ms, from 0.1145/0.1058ms).
float16::4 stays within 5% of 0.1003ms (device-bound control unchanged).
Falsification: if small-workload latency does not move, the floor is fixed device task-dispatch (SQ) latency rather than Python/Triton launch cost, and this change must be reverted.

warnings: msprof and simulator timing is diagnostic and is not eval latency.

Profiled steady-state inter-launch gaps (~130-150us) exceed the eval walltime (~100-115us) because profiling instrumentation inflates host time; only the intra-profile ratio of kernel time (1.5-7.6us) to gap time is used as evidence.
Instruction-level profiling was not requested because device compute accounts for <1.5% of walltime on the launch-bound workloads and would not localize the bottleneck.
open_questions: Whether the ~110us candidate floor is Python/Triton-launcher cost or fixed Ascend task-dispatch (SQ/queue) latency cannot be separated at metrics level: execution-trace.json contains only device kernel events and HostToDevice flow edges, with no host-side python/aten durations.

Why the reference reaches a ~22-50us floor on the same harness (native aclnn-style op vs a lower-overhead Triton launch) is not observable from candidate-only artifacts; no reference profile was collected.

The persistent kernel for float16::4 is reported with Block Num=40 while the seed host code computes grid=157 (min(256,max(40,2048//13))); whether 40 reflects a hardware AIV concurrency cap or a reporting artifact is unresolved and does not change the launch-bound conclusion.
